title: Service Contracts: Countersignature Window and Lapse of Unsigned Offers
content:
An offer of an AHL Service Contract binds nobody until the customer countersigns it, and the countersignature counts only if it is given within the window of the offered tier. This page fixes who signs, how the window is measured and what happens to an offer left unsigned.

## Clauses

- **Who signs.** Countersignature belongs to the customer to whom the contract is offered; no one else can give it on that customer's behalf.
- **The window.** Start from the offer date shown on the contract record and move forward on the calendar by the tier's number of window days. The date reached is the last day of the window. A countersignature given on that last day, or earlier, is in time; one given later is not.
- **Effect of signing in time.** The contract becomes active, the signing date is recorded, and the contract rates run from the contract's effective date.
- **Lapse.** An offer that has not been countersigned by the end of its window lapses. The system closes it as terminated, and the customer can then be served only through a fresh offer.
- **Reach of the rates.** Contract rates cover cargo received on or after the effective date and never cargo received earlier. The date on which the customer signed does not move that starting point in either direction.

## Window by tier

| Tier offered | Window after the offer date (calendar days) |
|---|---|
| `AHL Starter Service Contract` | 14 |
| `AHL Standard Service Contract` | 14 |
| `AHL Regional Account Contract` | 21 |
| `AHL Key Account Contract` | 21 |
| `AHL Global Account Contract` | 30 |
| `AHL Strategic Partner Contract` | 30 |

## Boundary illustrations (hypothetical dates)

| Offer date and tier | Last day of window | Signed on | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 March, Starter | 24 March | 24 March | in time; contract becomes active |
| 10 March, Starter | 24 March | 25 March | too late; the offer lapses |
| 20 January, Key Account | 10 February | 10 February | in time |
| 20 January, Key Account | 10 February | 11 February | too late; the offer lapses |

## Points of judgement

**A contract effective on 1 May is signed on 8 May, inside its window. Is cargo received on 3 May at contract rates?** Yes. The rates start on the effective date whatever the signing date, so cargo received from 1 May onward is covered.

**The same contract: is cargo received on 29 April covered?** No. Cargo received before the effective date never takes the contract rates.

**Can a lapsed offer be revived by a late signature?** No. Once it has lapsed it is terminated, and only a new offer can put a contract in place.
